identity.title: A Point-of-Care Integrated Detection System for Rapid Mycobacterium leprae Detection Using RPA/CRISPR-Cas12a and Lateral Flow Assay.

content.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Leprosy remains a significant public health challenge in many regions, and inadequate point-of-care (POC) diagnostics often delay treatment and lead to disability. We aimed to establish an optimized RPA/CRISPR-Cas12a POC system for M. leprae detection with integrated reagents, equipment and colloidal gold visualization. METHODS: The workflow comprised 1 min of tissue DNA release, 15 min of incubation and amplification in the instrument, and approximately 16 min for CRISPR detection. Assay conditions were optimized (200 nM primers, 37 degrees C, 100 nM each of Cas12a and crRNA), and analytical sensitivity and specificity against non-leprosy mycobacteria were evaluated. Clinical performance was assessed in 219 clinical samples and compared with Ziehl-Neelsen staining and PCR. RESULTS: The detection limit was 100 copy/muL for M. leprae DNA, with no cross-reactivity with other mycobacteria. Among 179 confirmed leprosy samples, CRISPR-Cas12a detected all multibacillary (MB) samples (100%) and 65.21% of paucibacillary (PB) cases, outperforming PCR (39.13%) and acid-fast staining (0%) and comparable to qPCR (63.04%). All non-leprosy samples were negative by CRISPR-Cas12a. CONCLUSIONS: This POC-compatible platform holds promise for early diagnosis, and the integrated reagents and equipment further enhance convenience for on-site testing in resource-limited settings, supporting timely intervention and leprosy control efforts.
